items.summary: In an unpublished per curiam opinion, the Fifth Circuit affirmed the district court's Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal of Kevin Berg's First Amendment retaliation claims against Officers Thomas Michael Rivas and Manuel Gandara and his Monell claim against the City of San Antonio, and affirmed the denial of his Rule 59(e) motion. The court concluded that the officers' actions did not cause an injury that would chill a person of ordinary firmness, and it began and ended its analysis on that second element. The source text is truncated, so the remainder of the opinion's discussion is not reflected here.

items.summary: In an opinion not recommended for publication, the Sixth Circuit affirmed the district court's grant of summary judgment to Walmart, Inc. and Sam's Club on Steven Campbell's Title VII and Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act claims alleging race discrimination, hostile work environment, retaliation, and constructive discharge. The opinion holds that Campbell did not establish a prima facie case on his adverse-action claims, reasoning that he was not qualified for the promotions he sought and that his transfer to Medina was not an adverse action because he had requested it. It also treats his FMLA interference claim as forfeited for failure to develop the argument in his opening brief. The source text is truncated before the opinion's full analysis of the remaining claims.

items.summary: The Fourth Circuit issued a published opinion affirming the Eastern District of Virginia's judgment in B.R. v. Fairfax County School Board, a Title IX action for damages brought by a former middle school student against the school board, school employees, and fellow students. The court held that the district court did not err or abuse its discretion in denying B.R.'s Rule 59(a) motion for a new trial, which challenged rulings on evidence and argument concerning whether she welcomed the conduct, the restriction of her expert's standard-of-care testimony, and the denial of a directed verdict on actual notice. The opinion states that the jury had returned a verdict for all defendants after a trial of over five weeks. Judge Gregory wrote an opinion concurring in the judgment. The text provided to this digest is truncated, so this summary reflects the opinion's stated holdings in its introduction and the portion of the factual background shown.

items.summary: The Fourth Circuit issued an unpublished per curiam opinion affirming the Western District of North Carolina's judgment in United States v. Antoine Depray Jackson, which imposed a 144-month sentence after Jackson pleaded guilty to possession with intent to distribute cocaine and to possession of a firearm as a convicted felon. Jackson's counsel filed an Anders brief stating there were no meritorious issues but questioning the reasonableness of the sentence. The court found the downward-variant sentence both procedurally and substantively reasonable and found no meritorious grounds for appeal. items.summary: The Third Circuit issued a nonprecedential opinion affirming the Middle District of Pennsylvania's denial of Charles Nelson Lenhart's motion to suppress evidence seized in a search of his home under a Franks v. Delaware challenge, and his motion to withdraw a guilty plea entered to three counts. The court held that Lenhart did not show that the affidavit's alleged omissions or misstatements were reckless or that they were necessary to probable cause. It also held that Lenhart did not establish a fair and just reason to withdraw his plea, noting that he did not assert innocence and that the alleged impeachment misconduct was unrelated to the charges.

The court held that the concerns Butuner raised did not fall within the categories of protected activity under N.J. Stat. items.summary: In an unpublished per curiam opinion filed November 24, 2026, the Eleventh Circuit affirmed the Northern District of Florida's dismissal without prejudice of pro se plaintiff Linda Chase's second amended complaint. The court held that the district court did not abuse its discretion by failing to sua sponte grant leave to file a third amended complaint, because Chase never moved to amend and had repeatedly failed to cure deficiencies. The court also found that Chase abandoned any challenge to the dismissal as a shotgun pleading and for failure to state a claim by not raising it on appeal.

Wetzel, No. 23-1699, a pro se action under 42 U.S.C. § 1983 challenging Barron's Administrative Custody confinement. The court cited its precedent that segregated detention is not cruel and unusual punishment per se and concluded that Barron satisfied neither the objective nor the subjective element of his Eighth Amendment claim. The excerpt also describes the Department's custody policies and Barron's review history, including his removal from the Restricted Release List in February 2023.

The plaintiffs challenge Texas Senate Bill 2024, which concerns the sale or marketing of e-cigarette products manufactured in China or other foreign adversary countries. Because the district court had granted leave to amend the complaint to add enforcement facts, the court concluded it could not grant any effectual relief, and it remanded the case to the district court for further proceedings.

items.summary: In an opinion filed July 30, 2024, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit vacated and remanded the Western District of Louisiana's orders denying the defendants' motions to compel arbitration in consolidated interlocutory appeals under 9 U.S.C. § 16(a). The court held that the district court was required to resolve threshold jurisdictional challenges, including personal jurisdiction, before deciding arbitrability, and it limited its review to the fully briefed personal jurisdiction challenge without reaching the merits. The underlying putative class action, brought by Jill Hines and Jim Hoft, alleges that the defendants, including Stanford-affiliated individuals and entities, the Graphika and Atlantic Council defendants, and the Aspen Institute, collaborated with government officials to monitor and censor disfavored speech on social media platforms.

items.summary: In this per curiam opinion, not designated for publication, the Fifth Circuit affirmed the district court's dismissal without prejudice of Jill Hines's suit against Stanford University and Alex Stamos for lack of standing, without reaching personal jurisdiction. items.summary: In MedEnvios Healthcare, Inc. v. Secretary, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, the Eleventh Circuit affirmed the district court's judgment upholding two Medicare audits that found a medical device supplier needed to repay approximately $2.5 million. The court held that neither the Constitution nor the governing statute required the Medicare auditors to include zero-paid claims in the claims analyzed through extrapolation. The opinion also rejected the supplier's remaining arguments, including its challenge to the disclosure of the universe of claims considered.

items.summary: The reported bill, titled the Consumer-Led Enhancement of Annuity and insurance Registration Forms Act or the CLEAR Forms Act, would add section 6A to the Securities Act of 1933, defining covered insurance contracts such as contingent deferred annuities and registered index-linked life insurance. It directs the Securities and Exchange Commission to propose rules within 12 months and finalize them within 30 months of enactment to establish registration forms for these contracts, including investor testing for contingent deferred annuities. If the rules are not finalized within 36 months, those contracts may be registered on existing forms specified in the bill until the Commission finalizes the rules.
items.title: 119 HR 10234 RH: Consumer-Led Enhancement of Annuity and insurance Registration Forms Act

items.summary: The reported bill, titled the Civil Investigative Demand Reform Act of 2026, amends section 1052 of the Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010 to limit civil investigative demands to violations occurring within 6 years and to require that demands include specific reference to particular facts. It allows an attorney advising a recipient to submit questions to the Bureau, sets response and return-date timing for those questions, and extends confidential treatment to petitions submitted to the Bureau. The bill also expands the grounds for setting aside a demand to include constitutional or legal rights and burdensome or duplicative demands, and makes the Bureau's denial of a petition to modify or set aside a demand subject to judicial review.
items.title: 119 HR 1653 RH: Civil Investigative Demand Reform Act of 2026

items.opening_verbatim: IB Union Calendar No. 784 119th CONGRESS 2d Session H. R. 4936 [Report No. 119–889] IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES August 8, 2025 Mr. Nunn of Iowa (for himself and Mr. Himes ) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Commit
items.summary: The reported bill, titled the Taskforce for Recognizing and Averting Payment Scams Act or the TRAPS Act, directs the Secretary of the Treasury to establish within 90 days a Task Force for Recognizing and Averting Payment Scams. The Task Force's membership includes specified federal officials, along with appointed representatives from financial institutions, digital payment networks, consumer protection organizations, and other stakeholders, and it is required to meet at least three times in the first year after enactment. The Task Force must submit a report with strategic and legislative recommendations within one year of its establishment, provide annual updates, and terminate 3 years after it submits that initial report.
items.title: 119 HR 4936 RH: Taskforce for Recognizing and Averting Payment Scams Act

items.opening_verbatim: IB Union Calendar No. 786 119th CONGRESS 2d Session H. R. 5889 [Report No. 119–891] IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES October 31, 2025 Ms. Pressley introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Financial Services Novem
items.summary: The reported bill, titled the Eviction Helpline Act, directs the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to establish within 1 year of enactment a hotline that provides tenants of covered federally assisted rental dwelling units with counseling, resources, and referrals related to eviction. The bill requires that information about the hotline be published in common areas of federally assisted rental dwellings and through other means the Secretary determines appropriate. Covered units are defined by reference to specified HUD assistance programs and to properties with federally backed mortgage loans, and the program terminates 7 years after enactment.
items.title: 119 HR 5889 RH: Eviction Helpline Act

items.summary: The reported bill, titled the Securing Facilities for Mental Health Services Act, amends section 242(b)(1) of the National Housing Act by striking subparagraph (B) and redesignating subparagraph (C) as subparagraph (B), which provides parity for licensed hospitals in access to the hospital mortgage insurance program. The amendments apply for the period beginning 9 months after enactment and ending 5 years after enactment. The bill also requires the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to submit a report to the House Committee on Financial Services and the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs within 5 years of enactment assessing the results and effectiveness of the program expansion.
items.title: 119 HR 7030 RH: Securing Facilities for Mental Health Services Act

items.summary: The reported bill, titled the American Lending Fairness Act of 2026, amends section 27 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act and section 205(g) of the Federal Credit Union Act so that, if a State adopts a law or certifies voter approval stating that the State does not want the federal interest rate exportation provisions to apply to loans made by its chartered institutions, those provisions will not apply to such loans made after that date. The bill repeals section 525 of the Depository Institutions Deregulation and Monetary Control Act of 1980. It also provides that the amendments govern the legal effect of any State law adopted or certification made under section 525 before the date of enactment.
items.title: 119 HR 7866 RH: American Lending Fairness Act of 2026

items.summary: H.R. 8957, the American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, as reported by the House Committee on Financial Services with amendments, would direct the Secretary of the Treasury to establish a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and a Digital Asset Stockpile within the Department of the Treasury no later than 180 days after enactment, for the custody of qualifying Bitcoin and other qualifying digital assets owned by the Federal Government. It requires annual reports to the House Financial Services and Senate Banking Committees, security measures, transfer of qualifying assets to Treasury title, and sales of reserve Bitcoin only under a Treasury rule, and it bars sale of digital assets resulting from a fork or airdrop for one year. The text as provided is truncated before the remaining provisions.
items.title: 119 HR 8957 RH: American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026

items.summary: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2021-11-08, which applied to all Pilatus Aircraft Ltd. (Pilatus) Model PC-6, PC-6-H1, PC-6-H2, PC-6/350, PC-6/350-H1, PC-6/350-H2, PC-6/A, PC-6/A-H1, PC-6/A-H2, PC-6/B-H2, PC-6/B1-H2, PC-6/B2-H2, PC-6/B2-H4, PC-6/C-H2, and PC-6/C1-H2 airplanes. items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR Fish and Wildlife Service 50 CFR Part 17 [Docket No. FWS-R4-ES-2024-0045; FXES1111090FEDR-267-FF09E21000] RIN 1018-BH42 Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for Peppered Shiner
items.summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the peppered shiner ( Miniellus perpallidus ), a fish species from southeast Oklahoma and southern Arkansas, as an endangered species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the peppered shiner. After a review of the best available scientific and commercial information, we find that listing the species is warranted. Accordingly, we propose to list the peppered shiner as an endangered species under the Act. If finalized as proposed, this rule would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species.
items.title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for Peppered Shiner

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR Fish and Wildlife Service 50 CFR Part 17 [Docket No. FWS-R2-ES-2026-2278; FXES1111090FEDR-267-FF09E21000] RIN 1018-BI86 Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for the Rio Grande S
items.summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Rio Grande shiner ( Notropis jemezanus ), a fish species from the Rio Grande Basin in New Mexico, Texas, and Mexico, as an endangered species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the Rio Grande shiner. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. We find that critical habitat for this species is not determinable at this time.
items.title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for the Rio Grande Shiner

items.summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus Canada Limited Partnership Model BD-500-1A10 and BD-500-1A11 airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report of multiple in-service failures of pressure regulating shutoff valves (PRSOVs). This AD requires revising the existing airplane flight manual (AFM) to incorporate procedures for reducing the thrust lever or shutting down the engine when the BLEED LEAK caution message is persistent, prohibits operation in known or forecasted icing conditions under certain minimum equipment list (MEL) provisions where the only operative PRSOV is an affected part, and requires replacement of affected PRSOVs with improved PRSOVs. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-13824; Project Identifier AD-2026-00525-T] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes AGENCY: Federal Aviation Admini
items.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 757-200 and -300 series airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of missing and/or incorrectly installed lockwire on backshells found during engineering validation tests in the wing leading edge and engine struts for high intensity radiated field (HIRF)/lightning protection features. This proposed AD would require inspection of the backshells at the left- and right-wing leading edge and nacelle strut for missing and incorrectly installed lockwire and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-13827; Project Identifier MCAI-2025-01826-T] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes AGENCY: Federal Aviation Administrati
items.summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-19-04, which applies to all Airbus SAS Model A350-941 and -1041 airplanes. AD 2024-19-04 requires a one-time detailed inspection of the engine nacelle anti-icing (NAI) forward bulkhead locating holes for elongation and loose fasteners and applicable corrective actions and prohibits the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-19-04, it has been determined that affected parts must accumulate at least 2,000 flight cycles (FC) since installation prior to the inspection to ensure that the inspection will detect discrepancies. This proposed AD would continue to require the actions in AD 2024-19-04 and would amend the compliance time for the inspection. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes

items.summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is issuing a final rule increasing two thresholds in its regulation implementing management official interlocks for purposes of the Depository Institution Management Interlocks Act (DIMIA). DIMIA authorizes NCUA to adjust the major assets prohibition thresholds through regulation to respond to inflation or market changes. This final rule increases both major assets prohibition thresholds to $10 billion to account for changes in the United States banking market since 1996. Additionally, the final rule removes a presumption related to depository institutions controlled or managed by persons who are members of a minority group or women.
items.title: Thresholds Increase for the Major Assets Prohibition of the Depository Institution Management Interlocks Act Rule

items.summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is amending its regulations for corporate credit unions by removing the requirement that a corporate credit union's asset and liability management committee (ALCO) must have at least one member who is also a member of the corporate credit union's board of directors. The final rule also removes filing requirements related to a corporate credit union's annual report and any management letter or other report issued by its independent public accountant. The intended effect is to reduce unnecessary regulatory burden and provide corporate credit unions with greater flexibility.
items.title: Corporate Credit Unions

items.summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is amending its regulations governing supervisory committee audits to eliminate unnecessary, redundant, and overly prescriptive provisions. The final rule is necessary to reduce regulatory burden, increase operational flexibility for federally insured credit unions (FICUs), and streamline the rules by removing requirements that are outdated or duplicative of other authorities. The intended effect of the final rule is to simplify compliance for FICUs without compromising the integrity of the audit process.
items.title: Supervisory Committee Audits And Verifications

items.summary: The Board partially grants a petition for rulemaking and proposes amendments to its regulations implementing section 208 of the National Trails System Act Amendments of 1983 to streamline the railbanking process. Under the proposal, the Board would no longer issue Notices or Certificates of Interim Trail Use during trail-use negotiations. Only after an agreement is reached would the Board issue an order authorizing transfer to the trail sponsor. Abandonment authority would no longer be prerequisite to railbanking. The Board would also confirm that by authorizing transfer the Board is not exercising any power of eminent domain or authorizing a taking.

It describes Federal actions including expansion of the Adoption Tax Credit, the Fostering the Future for American Children and Families Executive Order, the Fostering the Future Accounts, and the launch of FosteringTheFuture.gov. items.opening_verbatim: Executive Order 14439 of November 20, 2026 Protecting the Executive's Privileges and Enhancing Efficiencies in Federal Contracting By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America,
items.summary: Executive Order 14439 of November 20, 2026, requires all Federal contractors and subcontractors to notify the White House and contracting agencies of any pending or future congressional request concerning their communications or work with the executive branch, and to follow instructions on withholding communications that the White House or an agency determines are protected by executive privilege. It directs agencies to coordinate with the White House and contractors on responses to such requests, directs the Office of Management and Budget to issue implementation guidance, and states that agencies shall consider actions including contract termination and debarment or suspension for noncompliance. The order also includes severability and general provisions stating that it creates no enforceable rights, and it provides that publication costs are borne by the Department of Labor.
items.title: Protecting the Executive's Privileges and Enhancing Efficiencies in Federal Contracting
